@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@ +

The e2e mail helper's message type declares created_at and timestamp — KS-2029, e2e fixtures, TIER 2

+
What to know. AgentMailMessage in tests/e2e/tests/fixtures/test-helpers.ts now declares the optional created_at and timestamp, which the poll helper's date line already read. This clears the two TS2339 errors that sat there unseen, because no repository-defined leg type-checks tests/e2e. Type-only: no runtime change. +
No behaviour change. The members are optional and the fallback expression is unchanged. The proof was a hand-run TypeScript check (two errors before, none after, one planted control caught); no spec was run and no lint configuration covers this folder. +

@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@ +

. The e2e mail helper's message type now declares the two date fields its poll already reads (KS-2029, e2e fixtures, TIER 2)

+
What this changes. Before, the interface AgentMailMessage in Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/fixtures/test-helpers.ts declared received_at only, while the poll helper's date line reads msg.received_at || msg.created_at || msg.timestamp on a value of that type. TypeScript reported two TS2339 errors there (created_at and timestamp do not exist on the type). +
Now the interface also declares created_at?: string and timestamp?: string. Both are optional and type-only: no runtime line changes, and the fallback expression is untouched. Two members and a two-line why-and-ticket comment are added; nothing else in the repository changes except this page's fragments. +
Why optional members and not a deleted fallback: the mail API's real field names were not measured here. Optional members make the existing fallback type-correct without claiming the API returns them. Deleting the two fallbacks would change what the helper does at run time against a mail API nobody measured, so that shape was not taken. +
+

.1 Evidence

+
How it was checked. By a hand-run type check, NOT a repository gate: no leg defined in the repository type-checks tests/e2e (its package.json has Playwright runners only, and the root check:test-types covers five services). TypeScript 5.9.3 from the hoisted install, strict, on the file in the tree and on a scratch copy with the install linked beside it: +
    +
  • the unchanged file reads exactly two errors, (113,59) and (113,77), both TS2339, exit 2;
    • +
  • the changed file reads no error, exit 0;
    • +
  • a planted third undeclared member read on that line reads exactly one new TS2339, exit 2, so the check does read the file.
    • +
+
No eslint configuration covers tests/e2e (the file is reported as ignored), so lint did not run on it. No e2e spec was run: they need a running stack and none was up. The docs-fragments check, audit:gate and the check:test-types ratchet pass. +
+

.2 What it does not cover

+
Not measured here. Which date fields the mail API really returns; the e2e package's own Playwright resolution (it declares ^1.40, the root install is 1.61.1; the check above used the root copy); and any spec at run time. The workflow steps ci:e2e and quality:static run in systemTest/playwright, a different package; no file there imports this fixture. +
